items.name: Bodyweight Squat
items.description: A fundamental movement that strengthens the legs and hips and makes everyday tasks like sitting and standing easier.
items.setup: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart and toes turned slightly out. Hold your arms in front of you or clasp your hands at your chest.
steps: Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower down, as if sitting into a chair.
Keep your chest lifted and your weight spread across your whole foot.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, or as far as is comfortable.
Press through your feet to stand back up.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you stand.
mistakes: Letting the knees collapse inward.
Lifting the heels off the floor.
Rounding the back at the bottom.
items.easier: Squat down to a chair behind you (Chair Sit-to-Stand) or reduce the depth.
items.harder: Pause at the bottom for two seconds, or slow the lowering to three seconds.
cautions: Keep the range pain-free for your knees and hips.

items.name: Chair Sit-to-Stand
items.description: Standing up from a chair and sitting back down with control – an excellent starting point for leg strength.
items.setup: Place a sturdy chair against a wall. Sit near the front edge with feet flat, hip-width apart and slightly behind your knees.
steps: Cross your arms over your chest or reach them forward.
Lean your chest slightly forward and press through your feet to stand up tall.
Pause briefly when standing.
Push your hips back and lower yourself slowly to the chair.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you stand and in as you sit.
mistakes: Dropping heavily into the chair.
Swinging the arms to get up.
Letting the knees fall inward.
items.easier: Use your hands on your thighs or the chair's armrests to help, or use a higher seat.
items.harder: Hover just above the seat without sitting down, or use a lower chair.
cautions: Use a stable chair that cannot slide or tip.
Stand up slowly if you feel lightheaded.

items.name: Reverse Lunge
items.description: Stepping backward into a lunge strengthens each leg on its own while being gentler on the knees than forward lunges.
items.setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips or reaching forward for balance.
steps: Take a long step back with one foot, landing on the ball of that foot.
Bend both knees to lower your back knee toward the floor.
Keep your front knee over your ankle and your torso upright.
Push through your front foot to bring the back foot forward to standing.
Complete all repetitions on one side, then switch.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you step back and lower, and out as you return.
mistakes: Letting the front knee collapse inward.
Leaning far forward.
Taking such a short step that the front knee shoots forward.
items.easier: Hold a wall or chair for balance and reduce the depth.
items.harder: Pause at the bottom, or drive the knee up as you return to standing.
cautions: Use support if your balance is unsteady.
Keep the movement pain-free for your knees.

items.name: Split Squat
items.description: A stationary lunge that builds single-leg strength without stepping, which makes balance easier.
items.setup: Stand in a staggered stance: one foot forward and the other about a stride back, resting on the ball of the foot. Hold a wall or chair if needed.
steps: Keep most of your weight on the front foot and your torso tall.
Bend both knees to lower straight down until the back knee is close to the floor.
Keep the front knee in line with your toes.
Press through the front foot to rise. Complete the set, then switch legs.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise.
mistakes: Placing the feet in one line like a tightrope, which makes balancing hard.
Pushing up with the back leg.
Letting the front knee cave inward.
items.easier: Lower only part of the way and hold onto support.
items.harder: Progress to the Bulgarian Split Squat, or slow the lowering.
cautions: Pad the floor under the back knee in case it touches down.

items.name: Lateral Lunge
items.description: A side-step lunge that strengthens the legs in a different direction and opens the inner thighs.
items.setup: Stand with feet together and hands clasped in front of your chest.
steps: Take a wide step out to one side.
Bend the stepping knee and push your hips back, keeping the other leg straight.
Keep both feet pointing forward and your chest lifted.
Push off the bent leg to return to standing. Complete the set, then switch sides.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you lunge and out as you push back.
mistakes: Letting the bent knee drift inward or far past the toes.
Rounding the back.
Lifting the heel of the bent leg.
items.easier: Take a smaller step and lower only slightly.
items.harder: Hold the bottom position for two seconds.
cautions: Ease into the position gently; the inner thigh of the straight leg should feel a stretch, not pain.

items.name: Glute Bridge
items.description: Lifting the hips from the floor while lying on your back strengthens the glutes and the backs of the legs.
items.setup: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, and arms by your sides.
steps: Press your feet into the floor and gently brace your core.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top for a moment.
Lower your hips slowly back to the floor.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top instead of using the glutes.
Pushing through the toes instead of the whole foot.
Letting the knees fall in or out.
items.easier: Lift only partway, or hold the top position for less time.
items.harder: Hold the top for three seconds, or progress to the Single-Leg Glute Bridge.
cautions: If you mainly feel it in your lower back, lift a little lower and focus on squeezing the glutes.

items.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
items.description: A harder bridge on one leg that builds strength and helps even out differences between sides.
items.setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Lift one foot off the floor and straighten that leg, keeping your thighs level.
steps: Press through the heel of the planted foot.
Lift your hips until they are level and in line with your shoulders.
Keep the hips from tilting to one side.
Lower slowly. Complete the set, then switch legs.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
mistakes: Letting the hips drop or rotate to one side.
Pushing up with the lower back.
Rushing the movement.
items.easier: Keep the lifted foot hovering just above the floor with the knee bent, or go back to the Glute Bridge.
items.harder: Pause for three seconds at the top.
cautions: If your hamstring starts to cramp, stop, shake it out and reduce the range.

items.name: Wall Sit
items.description: Holding a seated position against a wall builds leg endurance without any movement.
items.setup: Stand with your back against a wall and walk your feet forward about 60 cm (2 feet), hip-width apart.
steps: Slide your back down the wall until your knees are bent, aiming for about 90 degrees or higher if needed.
Keep your knees over your ankles rather than past your toes.
Press your back into the wall and rest your hands on your thighs or let them hang.
Hold, then slide back up to stand.
items.breathing: Keep breathing steadily – it is tempting to hold your breath here.
mistakes: Knees drifting past the toes.
Pushing on the thighs with the hands.
Holding the breath.
items.easier: Slide down only partway so the knees bend less.
items.harder: Hold for longer, or lower until your thighs are parallel with the floor.
cautions: Choose a depth that is comfortable for your knees.
Make sure your feet will not slip.

items.name: Calf Raise
items.description: Rising onto the balls of your feet strengthens the calves and supports ankle stability.
items.setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, lightly holding a wall or chair back for balance.
steps: Press through the balls of your feet to lift your heels as high as you can.
Pause at the top for a moment.
Lower your heels slowly back to the floor.
Keep your body tall and your ankles from rolling outward.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you rise and in as you lower.
mistakes: Bouncing quickly.
Rolling onto the outer edges of the feet.
Leaning heavily on the support.
items.easier: Lift only partway and keep both hands on the support.
items.harder: Raise one leg at a time, or pause for three seconds at the top.
cautions: Use support for balance.

items.name: Sumo Squat
items.description: A wide-stance squat that emphasises the inner thighs and glutes.
items.setup: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width and toes turned out about 45 degrees. Clasp your hands in front of your chest.
steps: Bend your knees and lower your hips straight down.
Guide your knees outward so they stay in line with your toes.
Keep your torso upright.
Press through your heels to stand and squeeze your glutes.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise.
mistakes: Knees rolling inward past the toes.
Leaning forward.
Lifting the heels.
items.easier: Reduce the depth or hold a chair back for balance.
items.harder: Pause at the bottom, or hold a dumbbell at your chest.
cautions: Only turn your toes out as far as your knees comfortably follow.

items.name: Fire Hydrant
items.description: A hands-and-knees leg lift to the side that strengthens the outer hips.
items.setup: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
steps: Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, lift one leg out to the side.
Lift only as high as you can without shifting your weight or tilting your hips.
Lower slowly. Complete the set, then switch sides.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
mistakes: Leaning the whole body away from the lifting leg.
Arching the lower back.
Swinging the leg up quickly.
items.harder: Pause for two seconds at the top, or place a loop band just above your knees.
cautions: Use a mat or towel under your knees.

items.name: Side-Lying Leg Raise
items.description: Lifting the top leg while lying on your side works the outer hip muscles that help keep the pelvis steady.
items.setup: Lie on your side with legs straight and stacked and your head resting on your lower arm. Bend the bottom knee slightly for stability.
steps: Keep your hips stacked and your top toes pointing forward.
Lift your top leg to about hip height or slightly higher.
Pause briefly, then lower it slowly.
Complete the set, then turn over to work the other side.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
mistakes: Rolling the hips backward.
Turning the toes up toward the ceiling.
Lifting so high that the lower back takes over.
items.easier: Reduce the height of the lift.
items.harder: Hold for two seconds at the top, or add a light loop band around the ankles.
cautions: Rest your head on your arm or a cushion to keep your neck comfortable.

items.name: Jump Squat
items.description: An explosive squat with a jump that builds leg power and raises the heart rate quickly.
items.setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart in a clear space with a non-slip floor.
steps: Squat down with your chest up and arms reaching back.
Swing your arms forward and jump straight up.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and roll through to your heels.
Sink straight into the next squat.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you jump.
mistakes: Landing with straight, stiff legs.
Knees caving in on landing.
Continuing to jump when tired and technique fades.
items.easier: Do Bodyweight Squats with a rise onto your toes at the top instead of a jump.
items.harder: Pause in the squat for a second before each jump.
cautions: High impact: skip this exercise if jumping is uncomfortable for your knees, hips or ankles.
Check the ceiling height and your surroundings before jumping.

items.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
items.description: A split squat with the back foot raised on a chair, making the front leg work much harder.
items.setup: Stand about 60 cm (2 feet) in front of a sturdy chair braced against a wall. Place the top of one foot on the seat behind you.
steps: Keep most of your weight on the front foot.
Bend the front knee to lower your hips straight down.
Lower until the front thigh is about parallel to the floor, or as low as you can control.
Press through the front foot to rise. Finish the set, then switch legs.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise.
mistakes: Standing too close to the chair.
Letting the front knee collapse inward.
Bouncing out of the bottom position.
items.easier: Go back to the Split Squat with both feet on the floor.
items.harder: Hold a dumbbell in each hand.
cautions: The chair must be stable and braced against a wall.
Hold a wall or second support for balance if needed.

items.name: Goblet Squat
items.description: A squat holding one dumbbell at the chest, which helps you stay upright while adding load.
items.setup: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands. Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart and toes slightly out.
steps: Brace your core and keep the dumbbell close to your chest.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower down.
Let your elbows travel between your knees at the bottom.
Drive through your feet to stand tall.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you stand.
mistakes: Letting the dumbbell drift away from your chest.
Rounding the upper back.
Lifting the heels.
items.easier: Use a lighter dumbbell, or squat down to a chair.
items.harder: Use a heavier dumbbell or pause at the bottom.
cautions: Choose a weight you can hold securely.

items.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
items.description: A hip hinge with dumbbells that strengthens the backs of the legs and teaches you to lift with your hips.
items.setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs. Soften your knees slightly.
steps: Push your hips back as if closing a drawer behind you, keeping your back flat.
Slide the dumbbells down the front of your legs.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, usually around mid-shin.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you hinge and out as you stand.
mistakes: Rounding the back.
Bending the knees so much that it becomes a squat.
Letting the weights drift away from the legs.
items.easier: Practise the hinge without weights, or reduce the range.
items.harder: Do it on one leg with one dumbbell, holding a wall for balance.
cautions: Keep your back flat; stop the movement earlier rather than rounding.

items.name: Band Lateral Walk
items.description: Side-stepping with a loop band around the legs strengthens the outer hips and helps the knees track well.
items.setup: Place a loop band just above your knees or around your ankles. Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees softly bent in a slight squat.
steps: Keep tension in the band and your chest up.
Step one foot out to the side, then follow with the other foot, keeping the band taut.
Take the set number of steps in one direction.
Then step back the other way for the second side.
mistakes: Bringing the feet fully together so the band goes slack.
Standing up straight.
Letting the knees cave inward.
items.easier: Use a lighter band or place it above the knees.
items.harder: Place the band around the ankles or use a stronger band.
cautions: Use a band made for exercise and check it for damage before use.
